title: San Diego jobs and the Dreamland with McVea's Howdy Band
summary: Willard asks about the Blue Mouse Cafe in San Diego and the Dreamland Dance Hall at 8th and Spring where he played with Isaac McVea's band.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: How about San Diego. You worked in San Diego. According to the magazine article you showed us, you worked in San Diego with -- at the San Diego Pantages Theater and at the Blue Mouse Cafe.
Yeah, I did. The Blue Mouse Cafe, during the war.
It must be difficult jumping around.
(Inaudible) You've got so much stuff he's back to. Hearing about this I know what you--
It's hard to do it chronologically. And then it mentions another place in here that was on Spring Street. This is the Dreamland Dance Hall at 8th and Spring.
8th and Spring.
Is that the place you were trying to think of earlier?
Yeah, but I didn't play there long because I couldn't keep the job, you know. The band wasn't -- it wasn't stable enough. It wasn't good enough.
You played there with McVea's Howdy Band, is that right?
McVea's Howdy Band, yeah.
That was Jack McVea's father, Isaac, or they called him Satchel McVea too, is that right?
No, he was -- I guess they did call him Satchel. I don't know.
I saw that in one place.
Yeah, Satchel McVea.
Where did Howdy come from? Did they call him Howdy, too?
Who?
McVea.
Howdy McVea?
They said McVea's Howdy Band. Where did the Howdy come in, do you know?
I don't know where it came from. Somebody got ahold of it somewhere. You know, these things are very hard.
Yeah. I see what you mean. Well, we're just trying to get what we can here.
I was just trying to think what -- well, we'll go to something else and maybe this will come to me.
Sure.
The- it wouldn't say that I lied
(inaudible),-- that I didn't play at that place with the band, with McVea, when I did. I played with him.
